title: Sufficient predictive compression under finite samples

interface.source: n iid categorical observations from an unknown fixed law on K symbols, or a fixed controlled dynamical system
interface.target: predict the next symbol/future block under the same law, or predict action-conditioned tests under the same system
interface.shift_case: target representation may have an unknown binary alignment bit; only unlabeled target representations are available

claims.claim: The K-symbol histogram is sufficient for the unknown iid categorical law, and every posterior predictive future-block law under any prior depends on the sample only through the histogram.

cost.precision: exact integer counts and rational output under rational prior

claims.claim: The empirical categorical predictor has expected one-step TV error at most (1/2)sqrt((K-1)/n).
claims.scope: expectation guarantee, not a high-probability guarantee

claims.claim: Any exact summary of length-n histories that must preserve next-symbol predictions for every process over a K-symbol alphabet must be injective on K^n histories, requiring at least n log2(K) bits.
assumptions: all possible processes are in scope
claims.scope: does not rule out compression for a fixed structured process

claims.claim: Every environment represented by a finite POMDP has a linear PSR whose number of tests is at most the state count of a minimal POMDP.
claims.evidence: Littman, Sutton, Singh (2001), Theorem 1, PDF pp. 6-10
claims.scope: representation from supplied POMDP; no finite-sample acquisition theorem. Paper identifies action-conditioned PSR learning as open work.

claims.claim: With a hidden target encoder flip, source labels and unlabeled target marginals have identical observable laws in two worlds with opposite target rules; every learner, including one retaining raw source data and receiving infinitely many unlabeled target samples, has error at least 1/2 in one world.
claims.status: proved in report by two-world construction
assumptions: no target labels or cross-domain alignment pairs

cost.unlabeled_target_samples: no finite or infinite number distinguishes the two worlds

claims.scope: strict unknown-alignment no-go; do not generalize to known transforms or invariant-label shift models

claims.claim: Covariate shift by itself does not guarantee successful domain adaptation without further distribution-similarity or shared low-error-classifier assumptions; the cited lower bounds apply without target labels.
claims.scope: domain-adaptation hypotheses and access model from the paper

claims.claim: Ruan, Dubois, Maddison characterize idealized optimal representations under their assumptions via task discriminability and support matching, and prove a no-free-lunch result for source-only representation learning in their stated setting.
claims.evidence: Ruan, Dubois, Maddison (ICLR 2022), Theorem 1 §3.2 and Proposition 1 / Appendix Proposition 4 §B.3
claims.scope: discrete spaces and idealized population-risk model with stated generalized covariate-shift and Bayes-image assumptions

unresolved: Finite-sample PSR acquisition with explicit coverage, identifiability, conditioning, precision, and runtime bounds.
A nontrivial prediction guarantee for the actual target representation interface, if any is supplied.
Novelty or priority of the elementary two-world hidden-alignment construction.
